column1: # selftest-cache-inputs.tsv — the OPT-IN declaration table for the selftest pass cache.
# A suite with a row here participates in tools/run-selftests.sh's content-addressed pass
# cache: when the sha256 of (epoch, OS, bash major, suite path, the git blob id of every
# declared input) is already recorded as a pass on this lane, the suite is not re-run.
# A suite with NO row is ALWAYS RUN. That is the whole safety posture: under-declaring a
# suite's inputs produces a silently-skipped gate, which is the cardinal failure mode in this
# repo, so participation is opt-in and only the rows below carry the risk.
# TAB-separated. Columns:
#   suite repo-relative path <TAB> input repo-relative path
# ONE INPUT PER ROW, so adding one is a one-line diff. An input may name a file or a
# DIRECTORY; a directory contributes every regular file beneath it, in sorted order.
# THE RUNNER REJECTS, with rc=2 and a named error, a table that:
#   - names a suite it did not discover, or an input that does not exist (stale row);
#   - omits the suite ITSELF from its own input set — no suite may cache past an edit to its
#     own bytes;
#   - omits the script under test, where that script is the suite's `<stem>.sh` sibling;
#   - declares nothing besides the suite itself.
# The table is validated on EVERY sweep, including one running with no cache at all, so a
# malformed declaration reds locally rather than waiting for CI to read it.
# WHAT BELONGS HERE. Only suites whose cost is worth the declaration burden. Cost is measured
# in tools/selftest-suite-timings.tsv (which replaced tools/mutation-slow-suites.tsv in #641;
# the earlier landing set was chosen off that deleted file). Two suites have been considered
# and DROPPED because a composed set IS its transitive closure and cannot be enumerated stably
# from the suite: scenario-liveness-selftest.sh, and mutation-sweep-selftest.sh — the latter's
# case (j) enumerates `git ls-files '*.sh'` over the whole repository and its TSV-family lint
# greps the content of every tracked *-selftest.sh, so its verdict moves with any .sh file
# anywhere in the tree. Directory rows cannot express that either: the universe is the TRACKED
# set, while a directory row contributes every regular file beneath it, untracked included.
# Dropping a row is always safe: the suite simply always runs.
# EVERY SET BELOW WAS DERIVED FROM THE SUITE, not copied from a ticket. A suite typically
# reads more than an eyeball would list — exactly the under-declaration the self-inclusion
# rule cannot catch.
# AND THE SET IS THE TRANSITIVE CLOSURE, not the files the suite names. Neither of the rules
# above can reach depth 2: a suite whose own path and whose subject are both declared still
# under-declares if that SUBJECT resolves a third file at run time. The set below needed a
# depth-2 input the first revision missed: the scripts pipeline-cost-block.sh resolves
# beside itself. When you add a row, follow every `$here/`-style resolution out of every
# declared script until it terminates, and record where it terminated.
# DERIVE THAT MECHANICALLY, AND OVER PATHS RATHER THAN OVER SCRIPTS. Grep each declared script
# for its ${BASH_SOURCE[0]}- and $0-rooted path constructions and match every one against the
# rows below. Two things a prose reading misses. A resolution may target a .md or a .tsv as
# readily as a .sh, so a sweep scoped to `*.sh` mentions can be accurate and still incomplete.
# And a target the subject only tests for EXISTENCE is an input too: its absence flips the
# suite's verdict, while the key — content-addressed over the DECLARED rows alone — does not
# move, which is a stale pass. Both misses landed on this file's first revision.
# No `cost-block.sh` sibling exists — the script under test is pipeline-cost-block.sh, one
# directory up, which is why the sibling rule cannot be the whole of the subject check.
# gh-bot.sh is the depth-2 closure: pipeline-cost-block.sh resolves and executes it whenever
# tracker.bot.enabled is true, which the identity cases exercise. It resolves an out-of-repo
# wrapper under $HOME, so the closure terminates there.

# The largest declared closure in this file, and every row was read out of the suite.
# DEPTH 1, what the suite itself reads from the checkout: the gate under test; SKILL.md, whose
# line count case (f) asserts; tools/fixture-stamp.sh, which it SOURCES for the reaper's
# ownership stamp; the audit-toolkit hook, the writer half of the ledger contract case (d5)
# drives; tools/run-selftests.sh, the real runner cases (ic6)/(ic7) wire into a fixture config;
# and the two gate-ablation tables cases (ac1c)/(ac1d) classify against.
# DEPTH 2, what lean-gate.sh resolves at run time: branch-prefix.sh and resolve-sibling.sh (both
# sourced), operator-override.sh (also read directly by the suite's (yo) cases),
# claim-issue.sh, pipeline-cost-block.sh, and — through resolve_sibling — two cross-plugin
# targets. One is intake-toolkit's ledger-lint.sh, which milestone 1 uses to lint and reconcile
# a spec's Decision Ledger. The other is design-toolkit's figma-faithful-plan-reviewer.md,
# which resolve_plan_reviewer_agent() resolves on the armed design lane; the gate never reads
# its CONTENT, only whether it resolves, and it is an input all the same — rename it and this
# suite goes from all green to 39 failures.
# DEPTH 3, and where it TERMINATES: claim-issue.sh resolves gh-bot.sh, which resolves an
# out-of-repo wrapper under $HOME. The closure stops at the in-repo file, matching the
# cost-block block above. Nothing at depth 2 resolves a further file: lean-gate.sh makes seven
# self-relative path constructions, six of them the .sh rows below and the seventh that .md,
# and no script they reach makes another.
# DELIBERATELY OUT: node_modules/.bin/prettier, which case (fp5) uses as an opportunistic live
# oracle and SKIPS when absent — untracked, so it has no blob id to key on, and CI installs
# none. And .claude/second-shift.config.json, referenced zero times: the suite stages its own
# fixture trees, so no machine-local untracked file can enter the key. A declared input that
# does not exist is rc=2, and that file is absent on CI.
# tools/run-selftests.sh is already in the key as the runner's own blob id. It is declared
# anyway so the closure reads as complete standing alone, rather than requiring the reader to
# know what the key mixes in behind it.
